chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked him about a man who becomes junub in his garment: may he dry himself with it after his ghusl? He said: Yes, there is no harm in it, unless the drop of semen in it is still wet; but if it has become dry, then there is no harm.

The correct understanding of what this report contains regarding the permissibility of drying oneself with the garment when the semen is dry is that this applies if he does not dry himself with the place in which the semen is found, because if he were to dry himself with that place, the najasah would spread to him when it became wet.

key_terms.النَّجَاسَةُ: ritual impurity that transfers upon wet contact
key_terms.النُّطْفَةُ: the seminal drop referred to in the garment
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: becomes in a state requiring ghusl due to janabah

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to dry oneself after ghusl with a garment that has dried semen on it?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses a ruling on drying oneself after ghusl with a garment in which semen is present. It indicates permissibility when the semen has dried, while clarifying that one should avoid the specific area containing it so that the najasah does not spread when moistened.
